newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Buy Israel's Makhteshim on weakness.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Buy Israel's Makhteshim on weakness.

text.p: Carnegie Emerging Markets in a report released on Tuesday assigned Israel's Makhteshim Chemical Works Ltd a "buy on weakness" rating.
It forecast the world's largest producer of generic agrochemicals would show earnings per share (EPS) of $0.38 in 1997 and $0.47 in 1998, versus $0.34 last year.
Carnegie said that based on these forecasts the Tel Aviv-traded stock was currently trading at 16.7 times prospective 1997 EPS and 13.4 times prospective 1998 EPS.

"In light of (its) stellar share price performance and our concerns over cash flow...we would recommend purchase of the stock at below $6.00 against the current price of $6.32. Buy on weakness," analyst Stephen Levey wrote in the report.
Makhteshim's share price has risen 90.4 percent in the last 12 months in dollar terms.

Levey estimated Makhteshim would have a net cash outflow of $74 million in 1997 and a very small cash inflow in 1998, though he said he had not factored in the possibility of new acquisitions. The company had cash outflow of $144 million in 1996.
Levey said two Latin America acquisitions made over the last 12 months -- Herbitechnica and Defenpar -- were key to the future success of the company.
"The management of Makhteshim have recognised Latin America as a region where not only is competition not as intense as in other regions but also with a tremendous potential for growth," it said.
Makhteshim is a subsidiary of Israel's Koor Industries
